title: NonStationaryBrachistochrone: reproducibility package for controlled-rail brachistochrones in non-stationary spacetimes
description:
Symbolic derivations, numerical verification scripts, figure-generation code, and manuscript sources for controlled-rail brachistochrones in non-stationary spacetimes. The repository supports the companion studies of the FLRW and Vaidya sectors and of the conformal Kerr (Thakurta-Kerr) sector.

1.4.0 - referee-driven release. This version answers the Classical and Quantum Gravity review of the conformal-Kerr manuscript (CQG-116884). Every reproducibility finding in that report was correct, and pursuing them produced new mathematics as well as fixes.

Reproducibility, rebuilt. cap_full.py is restored: three computer-assisted-proposition runners import it, but it had been factored out of the prototype during development and never archived, so a fresh clone could not run the representative certificate at all. All thirteen figure generators are fixed: each inserted the repository root on sys.path while the shared style module lives one directory down, so on a fresh clone every one of them failed at import. That fix also exposed a silent bug in a turning-radius helper, which returned a grid point inside the forbidden region and dropped a curve from a published log-log panel with no error raised. Checksums and fitted slopes are now GENERATED rather than transcribed - the same two files had carried three different SHA-256 prefixes - by a single command, paper2/provenance/make_provenance.py, which also emits MANIFEST.tsv mapping sixteen artefacts each to one command and one checksum.

New results, all verified symbolically. (i) The local classification at the conformal stationary limit is a four-case law, not a trichotomy: the two marginal costates are dynamically inequivalent although the shape radical is even in the costate. (ii) For Thakurta-Kerr the selector is a conformal Killing vector and the rail drift along a geodesic equals A'/A exactly, so the control effort and the adiabatic expansion parameter are the same quantity. (iii) A sharp minimum-thrust bound, which diverges as an inverse square root at the freezing surface but stays finite at the conformal stationary limit. (iv) The Gauss curvature of the fixed-energy optical surface in closed form, with a threshold at rail energy squared 3/2 separating a focusing far field from a defocusing one. (v) Above that threshold the exterior optical surface is everywhere negatively curved, so no extremal carries a conjugate point and the cut locus is purely of Maxwell type - topological rather than focal.

Verification suite under paper2/verification/: nine scripts, 123 checks, each an exact symbolic zero or a high-precision convergence test rather than a tolerance. The Paper I suite introduced in 1.2.0 is unchanged, as is paper1/build_paper1.sh, which makes a clean checkout turnkey.
